name: optimize_java_dedup_nested_contains
description: List.contains per element -> LinkedHashSet; budget calibrated (naive ~3.2s native at n=150k all-unique vs ~0.01s, budget 1.5s); wrong-output broken loses insertion order via a plain HashSet
prompts: Dedupe.distinct(int[] xs) in Dedupe.java returns the distinct values from xs in first-occurrence order. It checks `!out.contains(x)` against a growing ArrayList before each add - a linear scan per element, O(n^2) overall and far too slow for large inputs. Rewrite it to run in linear time using a Set that PRESERVES insertion order (mind which Set implementation you pick - order matters here), returning exactly the same list for every input. Keep the class name, method name, and signature.
